name: CA-15
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Kevin Mullin running with large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
No polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The D+26 district, Mullin's incumbency and roughly $820,000 raised against an underfunded Republican challenger, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 96% all point the same way. With no contrary evidence, the fundamentals-based margin stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a closer race or unexpected outside spending against Mullin would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kevin Mullin, the Democratic incumbent, faces Republican Charles Hoelter in a Bay Area district that leans Democratic by 26 points. Mullin has raised about $820,000 and holds a large cash advantage, while Hoelter's campaign shows no reported fundraising. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Mullin roughly a 96% chance of winning.

The fundamentals strongly favor the incumbent: the district's partisan lean, the power of incumbency, and the financial gap all align. A low-turnout California general with a little-known challenger leaves little room for an upset, though sparse data keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
